- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.  
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is rising.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast slightly; if below, increase slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum shifts; adjust final 5–7 days to match sentiment trend if sentiment is trending strongly.
